Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• New-onset left-sided throbbing headache (24 h) with photophobia, no nausea/vomiting, no focal neurology.  
• Likely primary headache disorder; migraine without aura most consistent given unilateral throbbing quality, photophobia, female sex, family history.  
• Stress-related/tension-type headache also possible.  
• Low–moderate concern for cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (combined OCP use), subarachnoid hemorrhage, or meningitis; patient currently lacks red-flag features (sudden “worst ever,” neurological deficit, neck stiffness, fever).  
• Telephone management provided: start NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) with paracetamol, ensure adequate hydration, rest in dark environment.  
• Safety-net advice: seek urgent review if headache worsens, new neurological signs, fever, rash, or other systemic symptoms develop.  
• Arrange blood pressure check (overdue) and advise purchase of home thermometer.  

Management Plan
- Commence non-steroidal anti-inflammatory (ibuprofen; dose/route/frequency not documented) in addition to paracetamol.  
- Maintain good hydration and rest in a dark, quiet room.  
- Monitor symptoms; if deterioration or red-flag symptoms arise, patient to contact clinic/ED immediately.  
- Obtain blood pressure measurement at local pharmacy/clinic within next few days.  
- Consider follow-up appointment if headaches recur, correlate with menstrual cycle, or fail to improve.  
- No investigations or referrals arranged at this consultation.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Migraine without aura – High likelihood: unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, positive family history, female in 30s, symptom relief in dark.  
2. Tension-type/stress-related headache – Moderate likelihood: recent work stress, continuous baseline with fluctuations, absence of aura or neurological signs.  
3. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Low likelihood: risk factor (combined OCP) and new headache; currently no focal neurology or progression.
